candidates.decision_relevance: The analyses repeatedly compare negative 24–72-hour returns with short-window rebounds, but mostly provide endpoint summaries rather than a synchronized path. Historical hourly BTC and ETH prices, with timestamps and the decision-cutoff snapshot, would let reviewers assess rebound timing and whether weakness preceded or followed other observations.
candidates.evidence_reference: Daily outputs for 2026-10-24 through 2026-10-27 report mixed nominal 4h–72h windows, variable actual spans, and rebound-versus-drawdown uncertainty; weekly reviews also note missing granular price paths and freeze-time sequences.
candidates.metric_name: BTC and ETH hourly reference-price sequence with decision-time snapshots
candidates.missing_history_problem: Endpoint returns and overlapping rolling windows do not reconstruct the path available at each freeze, limiting sequence and hindsight-leakage audits.

candidates.decision_relevance: Breadth is reported repeatedly, but observations use different point-in-time membership hashes and proxy universes. Historical breadth observations with constituent membership, calculation timestamp, and method metadata would distinguish genuine participation changes from universe turnover and align breadth with price paths.
candidates.evidence_reference: Daily outputs from 2026-10-25 through 2026-10-27 describe top-100 breadth captures with differing membership hashes and conflicting proxy readings; weekly reviews identify missing quantitative breadth sequences and methodology.
candidates.metric_name: Point-in-time constituent breadth series with membership and methodology metadata
candidates.missing_history_problem: Unmatched snapshots cannot establish whether participation broadened or deteriorated persistently, or whether changes reflect constituent turnover.

candidates.decision_relevance: Multiple analyses have only a latest settled session or mixed single-session totals, while their hypotheses depend on whether flows persist, reverse, or precede price and participation changes. A timestamped history of settled BTC and ETH ETF flow observations would support that temporal comparison.
candidates.evidence_reference: Daily outputs dated 2026-10-25 through 2026-10-27 cite the 2026-10-23 settled row and explicitly state that it does not establish a current multi-session sequence; weekly reviews also note missing flow sequences and timing alignment.
candidates.metric_name: Settled BTC and ETH ETF flow history with session dates and reported units
candidates.missing_history_problem: A single settled observation cannot establish persistent demand or outflows, nor their ordering relative to price and breadth changes.
